The strongest evidence points to the tail device M5. It is the only transistor flagged as out of its intended region, and its width (0.42 µm) doesn't match its reference M6 (0.49 µm, same L). The mismatch lowers the tail current and raises its Vdsat, pushing M5 into triode at Vds = 0.28 V. That reduces the op-amp's gm and bandwidth, which is consistent with the low fc (+20% in M5 raises fc by 5.9%). The subsequent peaking and attenuation failures follow from the weakened amplifier. Restoring M5 to W = 0.49 µm (1:1 with M6) should restore the intended tail current and saturation.
